correctness.rationale: Exactly 64 times each sign-word count equals a full-field product sum minus six excluded-field products. Exclusions are bounded by 192, one-factor sums vanish, 15 distinct-pair sums each equal -1, and 42 higher-degree squarefree sums obey Weil with total coefficient 114sqrt(p). Thus 64N >= p-114sqrt(p)-207 >0 for p >= 16384. The packaged exact finite checker enumerates all odd primes p < 16384, using all admissible six-block starts and deterministic primality checks, asserts full support for p >=461, and identifies p457 as lacking precisely the all-residue word. It independently cross-checks Euler-criterion supports through p1009. This covers the infinite quantifier without extrapolating from finite runs.

evidence: Buchaev--Tsfasman explicitly evaluate lengths four and five, and record a general exact character-sum expression for all lengths but no six-word all-prime cutoff. Conrad proves uniform asymptotics for any fixed word with an error in sqrt(p); Wright proves general asymptotics for progressions, and Carella states sufficiently-large-prime pattern existence.

originality.rationale: The evaluated last exceptional prime 457 and universal full 64-word support threshold 461 are not stated or already implied without fresh finite evaluation in examined generic character-sum, asymptotic and length-four/five studies. Theorem 2.1 of Conrad and Section 2 of Buchaev--Tsfasman describe general counting ingredients, but neither evaluates all six-sign occurrence supports at every intermediate prime; checking all 1812 primes from 461 below 16384 and displaying the sharp obstruction at 457 is additional work. Searches did not locate a stronger published exact six-block cutoff, with residual unindexed-table risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed or unpublished exact six-word support census may already establish the value 461.
Bennett’s complete primary PDF was inaccessible; the accessible exact introductory quotation covers only homogeneous runs of length five.
An implicit evaluated six-word criterion buried in broad character-sum literature could make the threshold a corollary, though inspected closely matching works do not state it.

value.rationale: The largest prime failing to realize every mixed quadratic sign word of a fixed natural block length is a mathematically canonical cutoff. Length six extends past currently explicitly evaluated four/five-letter frequency cases and the classical five-consecutive-residue existence question. The exact value 457 and full occurrence after it, with an independently reproducible bounded certificate, provide genuine all-prime support information missing from standard asymptotic theorems; neither an arbitrary parameter choice nor a table recomputation of a previously established cutoff.
